steps.prompt: Your thesis makes three promises. How will the reader know which promise each body paragraph keeps?

cards.title: One paragraph, one part of the thesis
cards.body: Each body paragraph proves (or explains) one part of the thesis. Its first sentence, the topic sentence, names that part, so the reader always knows where they are.

cards.title: Linked topic sentences
cards.text:
Thesis: Our school should start a community garden because it teaches science, improves meals and brings students together.
Body 1: A school garden turns science lessons into real experiments.
Body 2: Fresh vegetables from the garden would make school meals healthier.
Body 3: Working in the garden brings students from different classes together.
cards.note: Each topic sentence uses a key word from the thesis (science, meals, together), in the same order.

cards.title: Your essay map
cards.body: When you check a body paragraph, the essay map marks its topic sentence: “links to the thesis” ✓ when it shares a key word with the thesis.

prompts: Which key word did you use to link each topic sentence?
What would happen if a body paragraph didn’t link to the thesis?
